note: Machine-readable scenario definitions. harness/k6/scenario.js reads this plus targets.json to run any (target, scenario) pair. Static metrics (cold start, memory, image size) are collected by run.sh around every scenario and are not listed here.

scenarios.title: Read one content record by ID
scenarios.intent: The single most common CMS request: a client fetches one record by its primary key and gets JSON back. Exercises routing, auth check, one indexed point lookup, and JSON marshaling.
scenarios.behavior: GET a single record by id, expect 200 + JSON body

scenarios.title: List 50 records (page 1)
scenarios.intent: The list view behind every admin table and public index page. Exercises a bounded, ordered scan plus serializing 50 rows.
scenarios.behavior: GET the first page of 50 records ordered by created time, expect 200 + array of 50

scenarios.title: Create one record
scenarios.intent: The write path: validate a body, insert one row, fire lifecycle hooks, return the created record. The scenario that stresses the DB write side and any hook/event machinery.
scenarios.behavior: POST a valid record body, expect 201/200 + created record with an id

scenarios.title: Filter by an indexed field
scenarios.intent: A query with a WHERE clause on an indexed column plus pagination, the shape most real API reads take. Catches missing indexes and N+1 relation loading.
scenarios.behavior: GET records filtered by an indexed field (e.g. category slug), paginated to 25, expect 200 + array

scenarios.title: Authenticate (token issuance)
scenarios.intent: Login deliberately runs a slow password hash (bcrypt or argon2), and this scenario measures how gracefully each platform absorbs a burst of logins without the hash starving everything else.
scenarios.behavior: POST valid credentials, expect 200 + a bearer token/session
